issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a method named printFarmSong() (UML and instructions), but both the template and the solution define and use singFarmSong() (and singFarmSongVerse()). This method-name mismatch between the specification and the code can confuse students about which method to implement and may lead them to add a method that is unused by the provided template or tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement to instruct implementation of singFarmSong() (and refer to singFarmSongVerse()) to match the template and solution; or (B) add a printFarmSong() method in the template that delegates to the existing singFarmSong(), and update the solution/tests accordingly. This alignment prevents student confusion about which method to implement.

issues.description: The problem statement refers to a Farm method named printFarmSong(), while both the template and the provided solution define and use a method named singFarmSong(). This mismatch in the public method name for playing the song creates a mapping confusion: students will look for printFarmSong() based on the instructions/UML but the starter code and example solution use singFarmSong(), increasing extraneous cognitive load and risking implementation/test confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement and UML to refer to singFarmSong(), or rename the method in the template and solution to printFarmSong(). Prefer updating the problem statement to use singFarmSong() to match the provided starter code and solution.
